messages:
Anya: quick sync — noticed some tenants seeing frequent route flips after the recent adapter-slimline. example: gold tenant with EU hint flips from latency route -> cost route multiple times in 10s. likely interaction between runtime penalty spikes and decision normalization.
Raj: saw that too. flip pattern looks like: compiler emits weights, runtime applies geo penalty then re-normalizes which amplifies the spike. hedged routes get overselected.
Mei: two possible fixes: 1) move full normalization back into compiler (single source of truth), 2) keep runtime normalization but change to sample-based smoothing + hysteresis. tradeoffs?
Tom: (1) gives strong invariants and simpler runtime logic. downside: old adapters that relied on runtime clamp break. (2) less invasive but complex: runtime needs to keep per-route EWMA and only adjust final weights if delta > threshold. more CPU and state.
Anya: I prefer (1) + compatibility shim. we already maintain versioned route blobs. make compiler emit `base_weights` and `normalization_version`. runtime must only apply either additive_penalty or multiplier but never a full renorm.
Raj: compatibility surface: route-compat v1 expects runtime renorm. it's ~0.8% traffic. we can add a `compat_mode: legacy-renorm` flag for that adapter only.
Mei: add tests: fuzz harness for weight vectors and a sim step where probe penalty spikes to 20x for 3s. assert final dominance doesn't flip unless penalty > configured dominance_threshold. also test tiny weight edge-cases: zeros, subnormals, all-equal.
Tom: UX/API change: publish normalization_version in route schema. New compilers -> version=2; older runtimes that don't understand it will fall back to current behavior. we should fail CI if compiler emits a schema not in allowed set for the repo.
Anya: telemetry items to add: `compiler.base_weights`, `runtime.penalty_vector`, `decision.final_weights`, `decision.hysteresis_applied` boolean, and `compat_mode` tag. those help debug flips quickly.
Raj: perf note: moving normalization to compiler reduces CPU pressure on hot-path decisions but increases route blob size slightly (~100-150 bytes/route). acceptable.
Mei: for safety, add a lightweight runtime guard: if runtime sees `normalization_version==2` and code path tries to perform full renorm, emit a metric and drop into safe-mode where it only applies multiplier. that prevents regressions while we roll out.
Tom: rollout plan: revert behavior in canary runtime first? or change compiler first? order matters. I propose: 1) make compiler emit base_weights+version (safe, no runtime behavior change) 2) add runtime guard to reject full renorm for version=2 (guard off) 3) ship unit tests+lint rule to forbid full-renorm fields 4) enable guard in canary 5) enable compat shim for route-compat v1 traffic.
Anya: timeline: I can land PR for compiler schema and lint rule today. runtime guard PR tomorrow morning. canary guard -> 1% traffic then 10% over 6h, monitor p95 lat, hedged selection rate, GPU queue length.
Mei: add sim: route-synthesis-sim with tenant mixes (gold/silver/free) and geo probes toggled. run overnight to collect deltas.
Tom: documentation: add an architecture note explaining normalization responsibility, and include sample JSON for v1 (legacy) and v2 (new). ops playbook: if hedged selection > baseline by 2x, rollback guard.
infra-bot: incident created INC-2026-119 for observed route oscillation, assigned to @Raj. link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-119
Anya: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/policy-compiler/pull/492 (schema + tests). tagging @Tom for review.
Raj: I'll prep runtime guard PR and compat shim. will link PRs here when ready.
Mei: once merged, I'll add the fuzz harness job to CI and a nightly sim. also add an alert for `decision.final_weights` entropy spike.
Tom: good. after this we should consider a longer-term change: policy DSL where compiler can mark certain routes as `non-flippable` for short windows (e.g., hedges for payment flows). can be a follow-up RFC.
Anya: agreed. adding RFC note to architecture backlog. thanks team.
